jobs: build one row of a nested JSON view
show the size of a large value
open a collection on its own
expand or collapse a collection from its row
summary: Takes a key, its value, the path to it and its depth, and returns one row indented by depth. A collection with items gets an arrow, a button that opens it on its own, and click, Enter or Space toggling it open or closed; a size column appears for collections and for values of a kilobyte or more, and a row with neither reserves no space.

jobs: append the visible rows of a collection
recurse into collections that are open
stop once the row budget is spent
add a button for more entries
summary: Takes a container, a collection, its path and a depth, and appends rows for its entries to the container. It shows one page of entries at a time, or every match and its ancestors while a search is active, and stops adding rows once the total row budget is reached.

jobs: show the focused data as a tree
say when the focused path is empty
say when a search finds nothing
note when the row cap cuts the list
summary: Takes the current focus and search state and draws the focused data as a tree in the view area. A path that holds nothing gets a short message, an empty result gets 'No matches' during a search or a short description otherwise, and a note is added when the list is cut at the row cap.

jobs: summarize the shape of a data set
list the top level fields with their types
show how full each record field is
offer buttons to open a collection
summary: Takes the current data and draws a schema view in the view area: a one-line count of size, nodes, depth and collections, a table of top level fields, and for each list of records a table of its columns with the share of records that fill each one and sample values. Clicking a top level collection opens it in the tree, and the icon buttons open a record list as a table or in the tree.

jobs: show a list of records as a table
use every record key as a column
keep rows matching the search text
say when data is not a record list
summary: Takes the current data and draws it as a table with a pinned header and a numbered first column, using every key found across the records as a column. Data that is not a list of records gets a 'Not a list of records' note instead, and an active search keeps only the rows where some column value contains the search text.

jobs: add a numbered row for a record
number each row from one
summary: Takes a record and its position in the shown list, and appends one table row to the body. The first cell is the position counted from one, followed by a cell for each column produced by the cell builder.

jobs: turn one field into a table cell
show a nested value as JSON text
keep full text for a truncated cell
summary: Takes a column name and returns the table cell for that field of the record in scope. A missing field gives an empty cell, a collection is written as JSON text, a null or collection cell is dimmed, and the full text is also set as a tooltip for when the cell is truncated.

jobs: show the focused data as formatted JSON
summary: Takes no arguments and appends a preformatted block holding the focused data serialized as JSON with two space indentation. The text in the block can be selected.

jobs: sync view tabs with the current data
show or hide the search box
refresh labels on the copy and cards buttons
rebuild the breadcrumb trail for the focus
summary: Takes no arguments and brings the controls and breadcrumb trail into line with the current view, search and focus. It falls back from table to tree when the data is not a record list, shows the search box only for tree and table, refreshes the collapse, cards and copy controls, and rebuilds the trail with an up one level button and a size and description of the focused data.

jobs: make a breadcrumb button for a path
dim crumbs that are not current
summary: Takes a label, the path it stands for and a flag for whether it is the last crumb, and returns a button that focuses that path when pressed. The last crumb is drawn at full strength and the others are dimmed until hovered.

jobs: redraw the body for the current view
refresh the controls before redrawing
summary: Takes no arguments. It refreshes the controls, clears the view area, and draws whichever of the four views is current: tree, schema, table or raw.

jobs: switch to another view
scroll the view back to the top
summary: Takes a view name, makes it the current view, redraws, and resets the scroll position of the view area to the top.

jobs: move focus to a path in the data
clear open rows and paging for new focus
scroll the view back to the top
summary: Takes a path and makes it the focused part of the data, treating anything that is not a list of keys as the root. It clears the open rows and the show-more counts, reruns the search if one is active or redraws otherwise, and scrolls the view to the top.

jobs: collapse or expand a pivot row group
redraw the pivot after the change
summary: Takes the key of a row group and flips its collapsed state, removing the key from the collapsed set if it is present and adding it if not. The pivot table is then redrawn.

jobs: show one tab and hide the others
highlight the chosen tab button
summary: Takes a tab id of pivot, raw or docs, shows that tab's panel and hides the other two, and gives the chosen tab's button the primary style while the others take the ghost style.

jobs: show or hide one tab panel
style one tab button as active or not
summary: Takes a tab name and, given the chosen tab in scope, unhides that tab's panel and sets its button to the primary style when it is the chosen one, or hides the panel and sets the ghost style when it is not. The element ids are built from the name with its first letter capitalized.

jobs: format a number as accounting text
show missing or zero as a dash
show a full-time equivalent to one decimal
summary: Takes a number and an optional flag that marks it as an FTE, and returns text. Missing, NaN and zero give a dash, an FTE gives one decimal place, and a dollar amount is rounded to whole dollars with thousands separators and negatives in parentheses.

jobs: fill the raw records table
clear old rows before refilling
summary: Takes no arguments. It empties the body of the raw records table and adds one row per record from the source list, in source order.

jobs: build one table row for a budget record
color variance and status by its sign
summary: Takes a record and appends one table row to the body with its fields formatted: the FTE to one decimal, the budget, actual and variance as accounting amounts, and a status badge. A positive variance is shown in an error color and a negative one in a success color, and zero stays neutral.

jobs: redraw the pivot table from current settings
group records into row and column cells
add subtotal and grand total rows
update the summary counters
summary: Takes no arguments and reads the field choices, aggregation and display toggles from the page. It groups the source records by one or two row fields and a column field, aggregates each cell with the chosen function, and rebuilds the table with optional heatmap or data bars, collapsible groups, subtotals and grand totals, then updates the summary counters.

jobs: set up empty cells for a row group
add a slot for each sub row
summary: Takes a primary row key and creates its entry in the cell matrix. With a second row field it gets one slot per secondary value found under it, and without one it gets a single shared slot; every slot holds an empty list for each column key.

jobs: place a record's value into its cell
skip records with no matching cell
summary: Takes one source record and pushes its measure value, zero if missing, onto the matching list in the matrix. A record whose row or column has no slot is ignored.

jobs: aggregate values by the chosen function
return zero for no values
summary: Takes a list of numbers and returns one number according to the aggregation chosen on the page: sum, average, count, maximum or minimum. An empty list, or an unrecognized choice, gives zero.

jobs: visit each sub row under a group
summary: Takes a primary row key and runs the scale collection for each of its secondary row keys, so every cell under the group is visited when the color and bar scale is worked out.

jobs: add non-zero cell totals to the scale list
summary: Takes a secondary row key and, for each column, aggregates that cell's values and adds the result to the shared list used to find the minimum and maximum for the color and bar scale. Zero results are left out.

jobs: compute subtotals for one row group
draw a collapsed group as one row
draw the rows of an open group
add a subtotal row for the group
summary: Takes a primary row key and appends its rows to the table body. It computes the group's subtotal for each column and its overall total from the values of its child rows; a collapsed group is one row holding those totals with a plus toggle, while an open group gets its child rows followed by a subtotal row when there is a second row field and subtotals are on.

jobs: gather one column's values across sub rows
add them to the column grand total
summary: Takes a column key and collects the values from every sub row under the current group in that column into one list. That list becomes the group's input for the column and is also added to the running values for the column's grand total.

jobs: build one detail row of the pivot
span the group label over its rows
add a row total cell
summary: Takes a sub row key and its position under its group, and appends one table row to the body. The first row of a group carries the primary label spanning all of the group's rows, the sub row label follows when there is a second row field, then come one cell per column and a total cell when grand totals are shown.

jobs: compute and format one pivot cell
shade a cell on a green to red scale
draw a value bar inside a cell
add the cell's values to the row total
summary: Takes a column key and appends one cell to the row markup, holding the aggregate of its values formatted as accounting text. With the heatmap on, the background runs from green at the lowest value to red at the highest; with data bars on, a bar grows from the center toward the sign of the value, scaled to the largest absolute value. The raw values are added to the row's list and the cell counter goes up by one.

jobs: total one column for the grand total row
pool column values for the overall total
summary: Takes a column key and appends a bold aggregate cell for that column to the grand total row. The column's values are also added to the pool used for the overall total.

jobs: hold the sample budget records
derive variance and status for each record
draw the first raw table and pivot
summary: Runs when the page loads. It defines a fixed list of 24 sample budget records by division, program, fund, object, fiscal year and quarter, adds a variance of actual minus budget and an Over, Under or Target status to each, starts the collapsed state, then fills the raw table and draws the pivot.

jobs: split one CSV line into fields
keep commas inside quoted fields
summary: Takes one line of CSV text and returns an array of field strings, without trimming. A comma inside double quotes stays in the field, and a doubled quote inside a quoted field becomes a single quote character.

jobs: parse CSV text into objects by header
skip blank lines in the text
trim cells and fill missing ones
summary: Takes CSV text whose first line is the header and returns one object per later non-blank line, keyed by the trimmed header names. Cells are trimmed, a cell missing from a short line becomes an empty string, and empty input gives an empty array.

jobs: read the two registry CSV tables
split list cells into arrays
keep blank value lists as null
summary: Takes a repo root folder, defaulting to the repo, and reads the registry and property CSV files from its docs folder. Each registry gets a file key copied from its path and a list of render targets, and each property gets its values as a list, or null when the cell is blank.

jobs: add a file key to a registry row
split render targets into a list
summary: Takes one registry row and returns a copy with a file key set to its path, kept as a separate key so a consumer does not depend on the path syntax, and with its render targets split into a list.

jobs: write rows as CSV text in column order
join list values with semicolons
quote only cells that need it
summary: Takes rows and an ordered list of column names and returns CSV text with a header line and a final newline. A list value is joined with semicolons, and a cell is quoted, with its inner quotes doubled, only when it holds a comma, a quote or a newline.

jobs: read and write the registry CSV tables
join and split semicolon lists
fix the column order of both tables
summary: A module for the two registry tables. It exports the line and table parsers, the registry loader, a joiner and splitter for list cells that escape semicolons and backslashes, the CSV writer, and fixed column lists that set the order rows are written in; a column missing from those lists is dropped on the next write.

jobs: set up the carousel kit
route arrow keys to embedded carousels
publish the carousel API on the window
summary: Runs once when the kit loads. It defines the arrow key routing for embedded carousels, the slide track builder, the fullscreen overlay, the shared entry button and the drill-down helper, then publishes them on the window together with the stack of open overlays and a top accessor.

jobs: create an element with attributes and children
summary: Takes a tag name, an attribute object and any number of children or arrays of children, and returns a new element. Empty string attributes other than class are skipped, an html attribute sets the inner markup, and falsy children are dropped.

jobs: add the carousel scrollbar styles once
reserve scrollbar space on wide screens
summary: Takes no arguments and adds one style element to the page on the first call only. It hides the track's scrollbar, thins the slides' scrollbars, and on screens 640 pixels and wider reserves gutter space on both edges of scrolling slides so their content stays centered.

jobs: step the innermost carousel on arrow keys
ignore keys typed into fields
forget carousels that left the page
summary: Takes a keyboard event and, for an unmodified Left or Right key pressed outside any text field, steps one slide in the innermost on-screen carousel that the pointer is over or that holds focus. The search is limited to the top fullscreen overlay when one is open, and the event is stopped when a carousel takes it.

jobs: register a carousel for arrow keys
return a function that unregisters it
summary: Takes a host element, a step function and a slide count, and records them so the host answers arrow keys. Registering the same host again replaces its entry, and the returned function removes the entry only if it is still the same one.

jobs: build a swipeable track of lazy slides
move the track to a given slide
release slides far from the reader
report which slide is showing
summary: Takes a slide count, a render function that receives a slide index and its element, and options such as start, keep, slideScroll, innerClass, snapStop and keys, and returns a handle with the track, a go function, the active index and listener registration. Each slide is rendered when it is near the reader and emptied once it is more than keep slides away, which defaults to 2, and every slide is exactly one track wide.

jobs: render one slide the first time
summary: Takes a slide index and, if it is in range and not yet rendered, marks it rendered and calls the render function with that index and its element. Out of range or already rendered indexes do nothing.

jobs: empty a slide the reader has left
run the release hook first
summary: Takes a slide index and, if that slide is rendered, calls the optional release callback with the slide, ignoring any error it throws. The slide is then emptied and marked as not rendered, so it can be rendered again later.

jobs: scroll the track to a slide
clamp the slide index to range
summary: Takes a slide index and an optional scroll behavior, clamps the index to the first and last slide, and scrolls the track there. The target is kept as the aim until the scroll settles, so repeated steps count from where the track is heading, and the default behavior is smooth.

jobs: track when a swipe has settled
schedule one update per animation frame
summary: Takes no arguments and runs on each scroll of the track. It restarts a 160 millisecond quiet timer that clears the aim when it runs out, and it schedules at most one frame update at a time.

jobs: render slides around the current one
release slides beyond the keep distance
notify listeners of the current slide
summary: Takes no arguments and runs once per animation frame after scrolling. It renders the current slide and its two neighbors, releases the slides beyond the keep distance, and calls each slide listener with the current index.

jobs: mark the page while an overlay is open
summary: Takes no arguments. It sets a marker attribute on the document root while the stack of open fullscreen overlays is not empty and removes it when the stack is empty, so the page layout can react to whether one is open.

jobs: build the track for a fullscreen overlay
decide whether the page can dock
lock page scrolling unless docked
build the overlay and panel frame
build the close or back button
summary: The first part of the function that opens a fullscreen overlay over a set of slides. It builds the carousel with its own key handling off, works out from a host hook whether a docked pane is offered, locks page scrolling unless the pane is docked, and creates the transparent overlay, the four row panel and the close or back button. The rest of the function is in later parts.

jobs: build the overlay header bar
add action buttons from specs or elements
keep the dock toggle in step with the host
add a menu under the header actions
build the previous and next buttons
summary: The second part of the overlay builder. It makes the position pill, the external link button, the action buttons (which take either specs or ready-made elements), and a dock toggle that asks the host again when the window changes. It then builds the title with an optional contents button, assembles the header, adds the menu hung from the header actions, and makes the previous and next buttons.

jobs: draw the pager as dots or a bar
hide the footer for a single slide
fill the optional subheader
assemble the overlay panel
hide the chrome while reading downward
summary: The third part of the overlay builder. It draws the pager as dots grouped by the index labels when there are 25 or fewer slides, or as a progress bar otherwise, hides the footer when there is only one slide, fills the optional subheader, and assembles the panel. When immersive mode is on it sets up the scroll and tap listeners that hide and reveal the header, footer and marked chrome; the part as given ends partway through that setup.
